title: Separating functional is coordinatewise nonpositive
statement: Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$, let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ be a payoff, let $u$ be a finite sample of columns from $Y$, and let $c : u \to \bbr$ be a fixed vector. Suppose $X$ is nonempty and $L : (u \to \bbr) \to \bbr$ is a continuous linear functional such that $L(z) < L(c)$ for every $z$ in the finite upper image $U(X,f,u)$. Then for each coordinate $y \in u$ one has $L(e_y) \le 0$, where $e_y \in (u \to \bbr)$ is the standard basis vector taking the value $1$ at $y$ and $0$ elsewhere.
hypotheses_covered: L is a continuous linear functional on u → ℝ
L(z) < L(c) for every z in the finite upper image U(X,f,u)
c is a fixed vector u → ℝ
